stories.headline: Alternative for Germany wins state election in Saxony-Anhalt
stories.body:
The Alternative for Germany party won the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. The party is also known as the AfD. Outlets reported slightly different final vote totals for the winning party. Al Jazeera reported that the AfD finished on top with about 44% of the vote. The Times of India reported that the party won 44.5% of the vote. Preliminary election results showed that the party won 43.8% of the vote. Those preliminary results leave the party three seats short of an outright majority.

Ulrich Siegmund is an AfD candidate in Saxony-Anhalt. Siegmund is 35 years old. He is a former fragrance salesman. Germany's domestic intelligence agency has closely watched the political group. The agency classified the AfD branch in Saxony-Anhalt as a proven right-wing extremist group.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke about the election results. Merz insists there can be no cooperation between mainstream parties and the AfD. Merz said the AfD victory was the worst electoral defeat his party had suffered in decades. His party is the Christian Democratic Union, known as the CDU. Merz said the defeat had shaken the CDU to its very foundations.

Voter support for the CDU fell sharply during the state vote. Outlets reported different numbers for the party's final share. The Times of India reported that the Christian Democrats fell to 18.5% of the vote. The BBC reported that the CDU vote share almost halved to 17.2%. Voters expressed strong dissatisfaction with Merz during the vote. An exit poll in Saxony-Anhalt showed that only 9% of voters approved of Merz's performance.

The state election outcome attracted international attention. US President Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the projected election results on Truth Social. In other European news, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni reached a political milestone. Meloni's administration has surpassed 1,413 consecutive days in office.

claims.text: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) finished on top in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt with about 44% of the vote.
The AfD won 44.5% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, while the Christian Democrats fell to 18.5%.
Preliminary election results show the AfD won 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, leaving it three seats short of an outright majority.
AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund is a 35-year-old former fragrance salesman.
Germany's domestic intelligence agency has classified the AfD's branch in Saxony-Anhalt as a proven right-wing extremist group.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insists there can be no cooperation between mainstream parties and the AfD.
Friedrich Merz said the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt was the worst electoral defeat the CDU had suffered in decades and had shaken the party to its very foundations.
The CDU's share of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt almost halved to 17.2%.
An exit poll in Saxony-Anhalt indicated that only 9% of voters approved of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's performance.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration has surpassed 1,413 consecutive days in office.

stories.headline: Thousands attend Belgrade funeral for convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic
stories.body:
Mourners buried convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade. Thousands of people attended the service. Mladic died in The Hague at age 84. He died while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. The United Nations war crimes court convicted Mladic of genocide over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre. Around 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were killed in that massacre.

Serbian Patriarch Porfirije personally officiated at the funeral service. The service took place at the St Luka church in Belgrade. Organizers provided free bus services from Bosnia and towns across Serbia for people attending. Fans of football club Red Star Belgrade displayed an image of Mladic before a match against Partizan Belgrade. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic did not attend the funeral. Vucic cited a scheduled meeting with the president of Uzbekistan.

The military honors at the funeral drew international criticism. An EU spokesman said glorifying war criminals, denying genocide, and revisionism contradict fundamental European values. EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos canceled a planned visit to Belgrade after the funeral. In separate local news, a canopy collapse at a railway station in Novi Sad killed 16 people in November 2024. That collapse triggered student-led protests in Serbia.

claims.text: Convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic was buried in Belgrade in a service attended by thousands.
Ratko Mladic died in The Hague at age 84 while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity.
The United Nations war crimes court convicted Ratko Mladic of genocide over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, where around 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were killed.
Serbian Patriarch Porfirije personally officiated at Ratko Mladic's funeral service at the St Luka church in Belgrade.
Free bus services were organized from Bosnia and towns across Serbia for people attending Ratko Mladic's funeral.
Fans of the Serbian football club Red Star Belgrade displayed an image of Ratko Mladic before their derby match against Partizan Belgrade.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic did not attend Ratko Mladic's funeral, citing a scheduled meeting with the president of Uzbekistan.
An EU spokesman stated that any glorification of war criminals, genocide denial, and revisionism contradict fundamental European values.
EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos canceled a planned visit to Belgrade following the military honors provided for Ratko Mladic's funeral.
A canopy collapse at the railway station in Novi Sad in November 2024 killed 16 people, triggering student-led protests in Serbia.

The reinterpretation of accepted historical facts.

stories.headline: Oil prices jump as shipping disruptions hit Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
Global oil prices rose as military actions disrupted shipping routes in the Middle East. Brent oil futures rose to around $97 a barrel. Brent crude is up 9% over five days. The price is also up 19% over the past month. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose to $92.27 a barrel.

Military forces reported attacks on oil infrastructure and vessels. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers. Iran's IRGC said it struck three tankers and three US-linked vessels. Saudi Aramco's Jizan facilities were struck for the second time in a month.

The disruptions reduced shipping traffic through a key waterway. Macquarie analysts estimated that around 7 million barrels per day of crude and refined fuels cross the Strait of Hormuz. That volume is down from roughly 20 million barrels per day before the conflict. Iran and Oman are in the final stages of negotiating an agreement. The two countries want to establish a temporary safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.

Fuel costs increased for consumers in several countries. The average US national petrol price reached $4.15 per gallon. US diesel prices reached over $5.90 per gallon. India's average crude oil import basket crossed $100 per barrel on Friday for the first time in six weeks. The price reached $101.07.

US West Texas Intermediate crude rose to $92.27 a barrel.
US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, while Iran's IRGC stated it struck three tankers and three US-linked vessels.
Saudi Aramco's Jizan facilities were struck for the second time in a month.
Macquarie analysts estimated that around 7 million barrels per day of crude and refined fuels cross the Strait of Hormuz, down from roughly 20 million barrels per day before the conflict.
Iran and Oman are in the final stages of negotiating an agreement to establish a temporary safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.
The average US national petrol price reached $4.15 per gallon, while US diesel prices reached over $5.90 per gallon.
India's average crude oil import basket crossed $100 per barrel for the first time in six weeks, reaching $101.07 on Friday.

stories.headline: US envoys hold peace talks with leaders in Russia and Ukraine
stories.body:
American envoys held separate peace talks over the weekend with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held discussions in Moscow and Kyiv. Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow first. The envoys then traveled to Kyiv by train from Poland. Putin declared a three-day ceasefire to ensure the safety of the visiting US envoys.

Zelenskyy held three rounds of talks with the US envoys in Kyiv. National security advisers from the UK, France, and Germany joined the final round. Witkoff said on social media that substantive progress was made. He said the progress included movement on scheduling additional trilateral talks. Zelenskyy said Ukraine will need a winter package of military assistance if the war drags into winter. He said that package must include Patriot missile systems.

The talks drew criticism within Ukraine. Ukrainian MP Lisa Yasko said Ukraine does not trust the talks. Yasko called the envoys' flattery towards Putin disgraceful. In separate human rights news, UN Human Rights Chief Volker Turk called for an urgent ban on fully autonomous weapons. Turk made the call after reports that autonomous drones killed people in Ukraine.

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Kyiv by train from Poland.

stories.headline: Israeli airstrikes kill dozens in southern Lebanon amid rising tensions
stories.body:
Israeli military strikes in southern Lebanon killed dozens of people over several days. Lebanese health authorities reported that Israeli attacks across southern Lebanon killed at least 27 people over a three-day period. The Lebanese health ministry said 13 people died in one set of airstrikes, including women and children.

An Israeli overnight strike hit a building in Kfar Rumman. That strike killed 11 people, including two children and four women. A second strike in Kfar Rumman killed an 18-year-old rescuer affiliated with the Amal movement. That second strike also wounded another person.

The military strikes followed clashes along the border. Two explosive drones were launched towards Israeli troops near the Ali al-Taher ridge. The Israeli military said it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in response. Near the Beaufort fortress, a Hezbollah member opened fire during a close-quarters encounter. Two Israeli soldiers were lightly injured in that incident.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun commented on the military actions. Aoun called the strikes a dangerous escalation. He said the attacks jeopardize the June US-brokered ceasefire.

A second strike in Kfar Rumman killed an 18-year-old rescuer affiliated with the Amal movement and wounded another.

Officially connected or associated with an organization.

stories.headline: Amazon cargo plane crashes past runway at Miami airport
stories.body:
An Amazon cargo plane crashed after overshooting the runway at Miami International Airport. The crash killed five people and injured five others. The aircraft was a Boeing 767-300 operated by 21 Air.

The plane was operating as Amazon Air flight 7598. It had flown from Cincinnati to Miami, then from Miami to San Juan. The crash occurred while the plane was returning from San Juan to Miami.

The plane overran the runway and traveled approximately 1,300 feet past the end of the paved area. It entered a perimeter area near where Tesla robotaxis were stationed. During the overshoot, the plane struck two vehicles. It hit a Ford van carrying seven contract cleaning workers. It also hit a Toyota Corolla carrying three passengers.

Investigators have started looking into the cause of the crash. The NTSB recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder from the aircraft. Safety features at the airport have also come under scrutiny. Miami International Airport is not equipped with engineered materials arresting systems at the end of its runways.

Amazon Air flight 7598 had flown from Cincinnati to Miami, Miami to San Juan, and was returning from San Juan to Miami at the time of the crash.

stories.headline: Seven dead after illegal hostel building collapses in Delhi
stories.body:
A building collapse in the Satya Niketan area of Delhi killed seven people. Reports gave different details about the age of the structure. Livemint reported that the building was 55 years old. Scroll.in reported that the building was 40 to 50 years old.

The five-storey building housed a boys' paying guest facility. The facility had two rooms per floor and two beds per room. A police source cited by PTI said the 55-square-metre structure had no columns or beams for support. Basement renovation work and water accumulation likely contributed to the collapse.

Reports also differed on the number of people rescued from the rubble. Livemint reported that rescue agencies rescued 12 people, of whom seven died. Scroll.in reported that 11 people were rescued. Scroll.in also reported that an estimated 30 to 35 students remained trapped under rubble. One victim was 19-year-old Arpit. Following his death, his family donated his corneas.

Police launched a criminal investigation into the managers. The property is registered in the name of 75-year-old Urmila Gupta. Her husband, 81-year-old retired Indian Air Force Sergeant Hariram Gupta, managed the facility with their 52-year-old son Mahesh Gupta. Delhi Police arrested all three family members. Scroll.in reported that the owner was arrested in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan.

Police filed a case at the South Campus Police Station. Charges include culpable homicide, negligence in upkeep of a structure, and endangering safety. An alleged agreement signed by occupants said facility authorities were not responsible for casualties or compensation. The agreement claimed exemption from liability for sealing, fire, heavy rains, earthquakes, or natural calamities.

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi, known as the MCD, had previously flagged the structure. The MCD identified it as an unauthorized four-storey building above ground level in a resettlement colony. Permission in that area was only granted for a single storey above ground level. Authorities suspended five municipal officials after the collapse. The Delhi government also ordered a citywide sealing of illegal five-storey buildings.

Legal and political reactions followed the collapse. The Delhi High Court directed the MCD to conduct an inquiry at the highest executive level. A bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia reviewed the case. The judges said responsibility extends to university authorities and the MCD. The judges said blame does not rest solely on the property owner. The court directed the MCD to audit paying guest facilities and hostels. It also asked Delhi University for details on outstation students and hostel capacity.

Political groups demanded official action. The Cockroach Janta Party released a list of seven demands. Spokesperson Saurav Das called for a probe into the larger paying guest mafia and the construction of government hostels. Das requested compensation of up to 1 crore rupees for families of the deceased. He requested 20 lakh rupees for the injured. Das questioned Delhi Urban Development & Planning and Education Minister Ashish Sood. Das asked why 13 district committees created after a June 2026 hotel fire were wound down.
